chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Asam, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

When a man is announced to his family, or they are informed that he has divorced her, and she observes her waiting period (iddah) and then marries another, and then the first husband returns, the first husband has more right to her than this second one, whether the first had consummated the marriage with her or not. And the second husband may not marry her again, and she is entitled to the dowry from the second husband because he made her private part permissible to him.

key_terms.الْأَوَّلَ أَحَقُّ بِهَا: the first [husband] has more right to her
key_terms.دَخَلَ بِهَا: he consummated the marriage with her

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a woman's status if her first husband returns after she has married a second man following a divorce or presumed death?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Akam* clarifies the mechanics of *Raj'ah* (reconciliation) in a triple divorce context, specifically addressing the scenario where the first husband reappears after the wife has married a second man. It establishes that the first husband retains priority regardless of whether he consummated the marriage, while the second husband is permanently barred from remarrying her and retains the dowry (*mahr*) as compensation for his right to her intimacy.
